_comment: Ablation: does the encoder do better reading the row as feature tokens (one token per column, FT-Transformer style) or as plain serialized text? Run with: python main.py --config config/text_vs_feature_tokens.json. Architecture, optimizer and splits are identical across the three experiments, so the only difference is how a row reaches the encoder.

experiments.name: feature_tokens
experiments._comment: Control. product_name receives up to 10 text tokens, then the five numeric and six categorical values each receive one feature token. ingredients is deliberately dropped for both representations.

experiments.name: all_text_matched_columns
experiments._comment: The same 12 columns the control uses, serialized as 'name: value | name: value' and read only by the text tokenizer. No numeric or categorical tokens at all, so a win or loss here is about representation, not about which columns the model saw. ingredients is deliberately excluded because drop_columns removes it.
